Hi Ben,

Apologies to surface this over email — our reconciliation flagged a large payment (USD 147,320.00) on 25-Nov that your lockbox posted to a suspense account rather than the open invoices it referenced. We attached our remittance advice (CortexRemit_20261125.pdf). The payment reference on our side: CP-20261125-4918. Bank says beneficiary reference included invoice numbers 8012, 8013, and a bulk reference "CP-Nov-24".

We see VAT posted to 0% in your ledger for the bulk, but the invoices are standard-rated. CortexPay needs the AR allocation corrected and VAT reclassified so our VAT returns and VAT recovery mapping align. Can you confirm:
- whether you can reallocate the payment to the three invoices and reverse the suspense posting,
- whether you will book a VAT reclassification journal or prefer a contra-revenue adjustment, and
- an ETA for the correction (we'd like this completed before your December close).

Thanks — attaching remittance for your team.

Regards,
Anita Rao
Head of Billing, CortexPay

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-28T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: CortexPay unapplied remittance — proposed allocation & journal (draft)

Team —

See the attached draft allocation spreadsheet (cortexpay_allocation_draft.xlsx). Summary: USD 147,320 from CP-20261125-4918 currently sits in SUSP-AR (SUSP-001). Cortex provided remittance showing three invoice-level references. CortexPay has confirmed mapping: CP->invoice 8012 (USD 49,240), 8013 (USD 48,540), 8014 (USD 49,540). VAT was posted at 0% across the bulk; correct VAT should be recorded at 10% which increases tax payable by USD 13,400 (rough delta).

Proposed steps:
1) Reverse SUSP-AR credit (date 2026-11-25) — debit SUSP-001, credit Bank Clearing (to neutral).
2) Apply payment across 8012/8013/8014 per Cortex mapping.
3) Post VAT reclassification journal: move the 0% tax lines to standard-rate VAT (move USD 13,400 from Tax Expense 9999 to VAT Payable 2100).
4) Record a one-time revenue mapping memo entry for P&L (to reflect that the original invoice VAT was not recovered correctly) — debit Revenue Clearing 4001 / credit AR adjustments 1400 for USD 13,400, pending exact treatment.

Open questions for Marcus: is the VAT delta treated as a contra-revenue reclassification (affecting topline) or should it be booked solely as a tax payable movement? If the latter, we may need an accrual to the tax payable account only (preferred for P&L neutrality).

ETA: if Marcus signs off by EOD 11/28 we can execute the reallocation in the 11/30 nightly AR run and send Cortex confirmation on 11/30 morning.

Thanks — draft attached.
Ben
attachments: cortexpay_allocation_draft.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CortexPay unapplied remittance — proposed allocation & journal (draft)

Ben / Laura —

Agree with the mechanics; suggested treatment below to keep P&L clean for this period:
- Post VAT reclassification as a balance-sheet movement where possible: debit Tax Expense / Other (9999) USD 13,400; credit VAT Payable (2100) USD 13,400. This avoids changing recognised revenue for the period.
- Record an AR clearing entry tied to the unapplied reversal and re-application: debit SUSP-001 USD 147,320; credit Bank Clearing 147,320 (to remove suspense), then debit Bank Clearing 147,320; credit AR 147,320 across invoices 8012/8013/8014.
- Create a memo journal to explain the adjustment for audit referencing (JNL-CORTEX-1126).

I'll attach the journal line CSV I'm proposing so the ERP upload can be staged (journal_lines_suggested.csv). Recommend we also run a quick tax impact check with Deloitte to confirm no amendment to past VAT return is required given amounts fall under de minimis thresholds.

If no objections, proceed 11/30 nightly.
Marcus
attachments: journal_lines_suggested.csv

Hi Deloitte APAC team,

Quick request: CortexPay remitted USD 147,320 on 25-Nov which posted to SUSP-AR in our ledger; the remittance ties to three invoices that were standard-rated. Our draft approach (see attached summary) is to:
- reverse the suspense posting, apply payment to invoices 8012/8013/8014,
- post a VAT reclassification journal (move USD 13,400 into VAT Payable 2100), and
- record a memo journal JNL-CORTEX-1126 for audit trail.

Can you confirm whether:
1) this treatment is appropriate to avoid an amended prior VAT return (given jurisdiction thresholds), and
2) the VAT movement should be booked as a pure VAT payable reallocation versus a contra-revenue item.

Attached is a short summary and our proposed journal lines. We're aiming to execute the correction in the 11/30 nightly run but will hold on final postings until we get confirmation from Deloitte.

Thanks in advance — please reply with guidance or a short note we can include in the audit file.

Best,
